But what you can’t see might matter most. The slope behind it. The water that used to flow through it. The ground it’s sitting on. These are the things that rarely show up in a property listing but can have huge consequences later. \n\nWith the support of Auckland Council, we were able to film in real properties with real hazard histories. Places that tell a much deeper story about what to look for when buying a home. The result is a video that walks through how to spot potential risks, and how to do your research.  \n\nThe conversation is led by team members across our organisation. From flood risk to earthquake vulnerability and unstable land, we talk through what to look out for at each property and how to research the natural hazard risk in the surrounding areas, helping home buyers make informed choices for them and their whānau.  \n\nA huge shoutout to Caleb Dunne, Alex Cartwright, Alex Bygrave and Andrew Martin for sharing their expertise in the film. And a massive thank you to Tanya Bidois, a passionate advocate for homeowners affected by landslides who adds her firsthand experience to the story. ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_youve-found-a-home-you-love-but-what-you-activity-7482250271050534912-G5pt"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural you a planner or policy professional keen to build your skills in managing natural hazard risk?\n\nWe’ve partnered with Victoria University of Wellington and New Zealand Planning Institute to launch a set of short courses designed to support better land-use planning.\n\nThese micro-credential courses focus on practical skills you can apply in your day-to-day work and can even count towards the new Master of Natural Hazards Science and Policy programme.\n\nDeveloped by Dr Wendy Saunders and others from across NHC Toka Tū Ake, the courses draw on our expertise in risk reduction and land-use planning.\n\nYou’ll learn about the laws that help manage natural hazards in New Zealand, such as the Building Act, Local Government Act, Resource Management Act and its replacements – the Planning Bill and Natural Hazards Environment Bill, as well as how effective policy is developed, and how to apply it to reduce risk.\n\nLearn more or register here:\n\nFirst micro-credential: The Risk 2024.\n \nWe were there to formally present the Fleur Templeton Award to winner Ursula Cochran, for her project “Living Healthily with Natural Hazards” – a mental health resource to support New Zealanders living with natural hazards. Ursula is actively working on the project after receiving the grant earlier this year.\n \nScience communication is critical to our mahi. As research funders, we want to turn the complex science we invest in into practical insights that helps New Zealand prepare for natural hazards – from everyday decisions around the home, to big choices about where and how we build. \n \nThanks to SCANZ for partnering with us to deliver this special award, which supports excellence in natural hazards science communication in memory of our shared friend and colleague.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_we-were-proud-to-be-at-the-science-communicators-activity-7478209206295244800-M247"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-07-01T00:59:10.134Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_this-week-marks-five-years-since-the-partnership-activity-7477888497110986753-vSTH","text":"This week marks five years since the partnership between NHC Toka Tū Ake (then EQC) and New Zealand's private insurers went live to make the natural hazard claims experience simpler and more joined up for homeowners.\n\nSince 2021, more than 23,000 natural hazard claims have been managed through the partnership, with more than $455 million in NHCover entitlements delivered to homeowners affected by floods, storms, landslips and earthquakes.\n\nWhile those numbers are significant, they represent something much more important – thousands of New Zealanders supported through some of the most challenging times in their lives.\n\nThis milestone reflects the commitment and collaboration of many people over the past five years. Thank you to the Insurance Council of New Zealand Te Kāhui Inihua o Aotearoa(ICNZ), our insurer partners, and everyone across NHC who has helped shape, strengthen and continuously improve the claims model that is based on homeowners at the centre. \n\nAs we look ahead, we'll continue building on what we've learned, strengthening our readiness and working together to support New Zealanders when natural hazard events occur.\n\nAA Insurance NZ, Ando Insurance, Chubb, FMG (Farmers Mutual Group), IAG, MAS - Medical Assurance Society, QBE Insurance New Zealand, Tower Insurance, Suncorp New Zealand / Vero Insurance New Zealand","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_this-week-marks-five-years-since-the-partnership-activity-7477888497110986753-vSTH"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-23T22:06:22.341Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_how-strong-are-our-stopbanks-across-new-activity-7475308296338497536-0HTd","text":"How strong are our stopbanks? Across New Zealand, thousands of kilometres of stopbanks help protect communities from flooding but predicting how they’ll perform in an emergency relies on knowing what they’re made of.\n\n“As communities have grown, stopbanks have been built to varying standards… in many places, we lack reliable information about the soils both beneath and comprising the stopbanks,” says researcher Dr Andrew Stolte from University of Auckland. \n\nWith funding from NHC Toka Tū Ake, Andrew is making it easier for engineers to quickly and reliably assess how stopbanks will fare in flooding or earthquakes – so that they can be strengthened before it’s too late.\n\nAndrew is our profiled researcher for June. Read more about his work, unique background, and his advice for future engineers at https://lnkd.in/e9AqtZBE .","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_how-strong-are-our-stopbanks-across-new-activity-7475308296338497536-0HTd"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-17T22:29:22.596Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_homebuyers-and-homeowners-dont-make-informed-activity-7473139758387503104-IuKi","text":"Homebuyers and homeowners don’t make informed decisions around natural hazards and insurance in isolation. They rely on a range of trusted professionals, like real estate agents and insurance brokers, in the moments that matter most.\n\nThat’s why we’ve been strengthening our connections with industry, working alongside The Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ) and IBANZ Inc. to make sure the right information is reaching people when they need it.\n \nA webinar we held with REINZ Education responded directly to members wanting clearer information about natural hazard risk around listed properties. Hamish Armstrong shared homebuyer insights, knowledge and resources to help support better due diligence conversations between agents and buyers.\n \nWe also delivered a webinar with IBANZ to grow brokers’ confidence around NHCover for land, recognising the important role brokers play in translating complex cover into practical advice.\n \n“Brokers often reach out to us with specific client queries, so we tailored the webinar to aspects of NHCover that are important to them. We’re following this up in September with another webinar that’ll help brokers support homebuyer due diligence,” says Brad Dahlenburg, who presented alongside Lynne Robinson.\n \nThis work is about extending our reach. By supporting the professionals homeowners already trust, we can improve understanding and identify where gaps still exist.\n \nIf you’re interested in collaborating on how we can better support homeowners together, we’d love to connect. Contact us: communications@naturalhazards.govt.nz","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_homebuyers-and-homeowners-dont-make-informed-activity-7473139758387503104-IuKi"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-12T00:24:56.269Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_how-can-we-make-buildings-more-resilient-activity-7470994513088458752-K1kR","text":"What happens after a building survives an earthquake? \n \nIn this piece for The Conversation, Dr Ashkan Hashemi, explores how we can design buildings that not only protect lives, but recover quickly with minimal damage. \n \nWe're funding research by Dr Hashemi and others on innovative connections that absorb earthquake forces without damaging the main structure, and new approaches to make timber houses (the most common type in New Zealand) easier and faster to repair. \n \nHave a read: https://lnkd.in/etASJzJu","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_how-can-we-make-buildings-more-resilient-activity-7470994513088458752-K1kR"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-10T22:46:02.856Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_the-researcher-whos-shaken-up-earth-sciences-activity-7470607238689140737-dGaU","text":"As Emeritus Prof Tim Stern retires, we’re reflecting on research we’ve been proud to support over many years. Most recently, our funding helped underpin work mapping the Wellington basin in much greater detail - improving understanding of why shaking was amplified in parts of the city in the 2016 Kaikōura earthquake and supporting better hazard modelling and resilience planning for Wellington. We also backed earlier research linked to the Hikurangi subduction zone and Alpine Fault, helping build New Zealand’s understanding of the tectonic processes that drive earthquake risk. \n \nWe thank Tim for his longstanding contribution to earth science in Aotearoa New Zealand. 👏 \n \nRead more about Tim's distinguished career in this story from Victoria University of Wellington: https://lnkd.in/eMgdSwnM","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_the-researcher-whos-shaken-up-earth-sciences-activity-7470607238689140737-dGaU"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-10T00:03:14.461Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_welcome-to-the-natural-hazards-portal-te-activity-7470264277178867712-Voc3","text":"Today we're excited to launch the new Natural Hazards Portal.\n \nThe Portal brings together natural hazard and claims information in one place, helping New Zealanders better understand the natural hazards that could affect their homes and communities.\n \nThis upgrade introduces a faster, clearer and easier-to-use experience, with improved mobile functionality, simpler navigation, and new features designed to make complex information more accessible and useful.\n \nFor the first time, people can now explore natural hazard maps for the Bay of Plenty region alongside EQCover and NHCover settled claims dating back to 1997, with more regions to be added over time. The Portal also includes the ability to explore natural hazard scenarios and new content to help users understand concepts such as hazard exposure, risk and uncertainty.\n \nThis is an important step towards our long-term vision of creating a leading source of natural hazard risk information and insights. The Portal will continue to grow over time as new data, tools and functionality become available.\n \nA project of this scale is only possible through collaboration. We'd like to sincerely thank our delivery partner Somar Digital, the input from Earth Sciences New Zealand and our Bay of Plenty pilot partners Toi Moana Bay of Plenty Regional Council and Tauranga City Council, whose expertise, support and willingness to innovate helped make this milestone possible. We are particularly grateful for the partnership shown by both councils in helping us test and refine how hazard information can be presented in a way that is useful and meaningful for communities.\n \nWhether you're a homeowner, homebuyer, planner, researcher, or simply curious about the natural hazards that could affect your community, the Portal is a great place to start.\n \nTake a look and let us know what you think: https://lnkd.in/dkWJh_kv","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_welcome-to-the-natural-hazards-portal-te-activity-7470264277178867712-Voc3"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-07T21:06:51.906Z","headline":"","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_were-proud-to-launch-our-latest-digital-activity-7469495115003277312-k54x","text":"We’re proud to launch our latest digital campaign on earthquake preparedness. In New Zealand, the powerful forces that shape our landscapes also mean earthquakes are a part of life here – making being prepared an important part of how we live. \n \nAt the heart of ' Quake safe your place. Don't wait for the WOAH!!' is a simple message: we don’t need to live scared of earthquakes, but we do need to be ready for them – and every step we take now helps. \n\nNew research shows earthquakes are still Kiwis’ top natural hazard concern, and most believe they could seriously damage our homes. \n\n👉 70% of Kiwis are aware of the actions they can take \n👉 Way fewer actually do it. \n\nThis campaign encourages people to take practical steps now, before the next big shake.\n\nThe campaign is on several channels across the next few weeks, including national TV, radio, billboards, digital platforms and social media.\n\nHead to our Facebook page to find more content to share with your audiences.\n\nThanks to VML and Eyes and Ears for helping to bring this important message to life.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_were-proud-to-launch-our-latest-digital-activity-7469495115003277312-k54x"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission","address":{"type":"PostalAddress","streetAddress":"100 Willis St","addressLocality":"Wellington","postalCode":"6011","addressCountry":"NZ"},"description":"The Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake (formerly the Earthquake Commission) exists to reduce the impact of natural hazards on people, property, and the community. We do this is by providing natural hazards cover for homes and residential land, for a range of natural hazards.         attributed-text-segment-list__content-truncated" dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">You’ve found a home you love. But what you can’t see might matter most. The slope behind it. The water that used to flow through it. The ground it’s sitting on. These are the things that rarely show up in a property listing but can have huge consequences later. 

With the support of <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/auckland-council?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Auckland Council</a>, we were able to film in real properties with real hazard histories. Places that tell a much deeper story about what to look for when buying a home. The result is a video that walks through how to spot potential risks, and how to do your research.  

The conversation is led by team members across our organisation. From flood risk to earthquake vulnerability and unstable land, we talk through what to look out for at each property and how to research the natural hazard risk in the surrounding areas, helping home buyers make informed choices for them and their whānau.  

A huge shoutout to <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/calebdunne?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Caleb Dunne</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/alexcartwright1?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Alex Cartwright</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/alex-bygrave-a0406971?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Alex Bygrave</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/andrew-martin-7b0828223?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Andrew Martin</a> for sharing their expertise in the film. And a massive thank you to Tanya Bidois, a passionate advocate for homeowners affected by landslides who adds her firsthand experience to the story. </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Are you a planner or policy professional keen to build your skills in managing natural hazard risk?

We’ve partnered with <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/victoria-university-of-wellington-a036a8324?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Victoria University of Wellington</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/new-zealand-planning-institute?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>New Zealand Planning Institute</a> to launch a set of short courses designed to support better land-use planning.

These micro-credential courses focus on practical skills you can apply in your day-to-day work and can even count towards the new Master of Natural Hazards Science and Policy programme.

Developed by Dr <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/wendy-saunders-b9463228?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Wendy Saunders</a> and others from across NHC Toka Tū Ake, the courses draw on our expertise in risk reduction and land-use planning.

You’ll learn about the laws that help manage natural hazards in New Zealand, such as the Building Act, Local Government Act, Resource Management Act and its replacements – the Planning Bill and Natural Hazards Environment Bill, as well as how effective policy is developed, and how to apply it to reduce risk.

Learn more or register here:

First micro-credential: The Risk Management System and Natural Hazard Management: <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/eq-WCg6h?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/eq-WCg6h</a>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">We were proud to be at the <a class="link" href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/science-communicator-s-association-of-new-zealand-scanz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Science Communicators' Association of New Zealand SCANZ</a> conference to commemorate Fleur Templeton, a science communicator in our team and a member of SCANZ, who passed away in 2024.
 
We were there to formally present the Fleur Templeton Award to winner <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/ursula-cochran-35789784?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Ursula Cochran</a>, for her project “Living Healthily with Natural Hazards” – a mental health resource to support New Zealanders living with natural hazards. Ursula is actively working on the project after receiving the grant earlier this year.
 
Science communication is critical to our mahi. As research funders, we want to turn the complex science we invest in into practical insights that helps New Zealand prepare for natural hazards – from everyday decisions around the home, to big choices about where and how we build. 
 
Thanks to SCANZ for partnering with us to deliver this special award, which supports excellence in natural hazards science communication in memory of our shared friend and colleague.</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">This week marks five years since the partnership between NHC Toka Tū Ake (then EQC) and New Zealand's private insurers went live to make the natural hazard claims experience simpler and more joined up for homeowners.

Since 2021, more than 23,000 natural hazard claims have been managed through the partnership, with more than $455 million in NHCover entitlements delivered to homeowners affected by floods, storms, landslips and earthquakes.

While those numbers are significant, they represent something much more important – thousands of New Zealanders supported through some of the most challenging times in their lives.

This milestone reflects the commitment and collaboration of many people over the past five years. Thank you to the <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/icnz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Insurance Council of New Zealand Te Kāhui Inihua o Aotearoa(ICNZ)</a>, our insurer partners, and everyone across NHC who has helped shape, strengthen and continuously improve the claims model that is based on homeowners at the centre. 

As we look ahead, we'll continue building on what we've learned, strengthening our readiness and working together to support New Zealanders when natural hazard events occur.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">How strong are our stopbanks? Across New Zealand, thousands of kilometres of stopbanks help protect communities from flooding but predicting how they’ll perform in an emergency relies on knowing what they’re made of.

Andrew is our profiled researcher for June.     <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Homebuyers and homeowners don’t make informed decisions around natural hazards and insurance in isolation. They rely on a range of trusted professionals, like real estate agents and insurance brokers, in the moments that matter most.

That’s why we’ve been strengthening our connections with industry, working alongside <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/reinz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>The Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ)</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/ibanz-inc-?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>IBANZ Inc.</a> to make sure the right information is reaching people when they need it.
 
A webinar we held with REINZ Education responded directly to members wanting clearer information about natural hazard risk around listed properties. <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/hamish-armstrong-a7858833?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Hamish Armstrong</a> shared homebuyer insights, knowledge and resources to help support better due diligence conversations between agents and buyers.
 
We also delivered a webinar with IBANZ to grow brokers’ confidence around NHCover for land, recognising the important role brokers play in translating complex cover into practical advice.
 
“Brokers often reach out to us with specific client queries, so we tailored the webinar to aspects of NHCover that are important to them. We’re following this up in September with another webinar that’ll help brokers support homebuyer due diligence,” says <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/brad-dahlenburg-913470263?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Brad Dahlenburg</a>, who presented alongside Lynne Robinson.
 
This work is about extending our reach. By supporting the professionals homeowners already trust, we can improve understanding and identify where gaps still exist.
 
If you’re interested in collaborating on how we can better support homeowners together, we’d love to connect. Contact us: <a class="link" href="mailto:communications@naturalhazards.govt.nz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>communications@naturalhazards.govt.nz</a></p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Today we're excited to launch the new Natural Hazards Portal.
 
The Portal brings together natural hazard and claims information in one place, helping New Zealanders better understand the natural hazards that could affect their homes and communities.
 
This upgrade introduces a faster, clearer and easier-to-use experience, with improved mobile functionality, simpler navigation, and new features designed to make complex information more accessible and useful.
 
For the first time, people can now explore natural hazard maps for the Bay of Plenty region alongside EQCover and NHCover settled claims dating back to 1997, with more regions to be added over time. The Portal also includes the ability to explore natural hazard scenarios and new content to help users understand concepts such as hazard exposure, risk and uncertainty.
 
This is an important step towards our long-term vision of creating a leading source of natural hazard risk information and insights. The Portal will continue to grow over time as new data, tools and functionality become available.
 
A project of this scale is only possible through collaboration. We'd like to sincerely thank our delivery partner <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/somar-digital?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Somar Digital</a>, the input from <a class="link" href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/earthsciencesnz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Earth Sciences New Zealand</a> and our Bay of Plenty pilot partners <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/bay-of-plenty-regional-council?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Toi Moana Bay of Plenty Regional Council</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tauranga-city-council?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Tauranga City Council</a>, whose expertise, support and willingness to innovate helped make this milestone possible. We are particularly grateful for the partnership shown by both councils in helping us test and refine how hazard information can be presented in a way that is useful and meaningful for communities.
 
Whether you're a homeowner, homebuyer, planner, researcher, or simply curious about the natural hazards that could affect your community, the Portal is a great place to start.

        attributed-text-segment-list__content-truncated" dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">We’re proud to launch our latest digital campaign on earthquake preparedness. In New Zealand, the powerful forces that shape our landscapes also mean earthquakes are a part of life here – making being prepared an important part of how we live. 
 
At the heart of ' Quake safe your place. Don't wait for the WOAH!!' is a simple message: we don’t need to live scared of earthquakes, but we do need to be ready for them – and every step we take now helps. 

New research shows earthquakes are still Kiwis’ top natural hazard concern, and most believe they could seriously damage our homes. 

👉 70% of Kiwis are aware of the actions they can take 
👉 Way fewer actually do it. 

This campaign encourages people to take practical steps now, before the next big shake.

The campaign is on several channels across the next few weeks, including national TV, radio, billboards, digital platforms and social media.

Head to our Facebook page to find more content to share with your audiences.
